issues.description: The problem specification contains conflicting information about the return type of messageOnMilk(): the UML for the Milkable interface declares messageOnMilk(): boolean and the textual requirement states it should return true/false when milking succeeds, while elsewhere in the same UML (Seal class) and in the solution implementation Milkable.messageOnMilk() and the implementing classes (Goat, Seal) use String return types. The template Main also uses Milkable and prints m.messageOnMilk(), which aligns with a String. This mismatch between boolean and String will confuse students and prevent a consistent implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification, UML, template usage, and solution consistent. Either: (A) change the UML and textual description to specify messageOnMilk() returns a String (e.g. a human-readable milking message) and update the sentence that currently says it should return true/false; or (B) change the solution (Milkable interface and all implementing classes) to return boolean and adjust places that print messageOnMilk() accordingly. Option A is recommended because the template Main and solution already treat messageOnMilk() as a printable String.

issues.description: Inconsistent specification of the Milkable.messageOnMilk() API across artifacts: the UML fragment in problem_statement.md declares Milkable.messageOnMilk() as returning boolean, the textual task description also says it should return true/false, but the class diagrams (Seal/Goat) and the provided solution implement messageOnMilk() and the Milkable interface as returning a String (e.g. "Seal [name] is milked"). This mismatch between boolean vs. String for the same conceptual method will confuse students about the expected return type and how to implement and use Milkable.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the mismatch by choosing one return type for messageOnMilk() across all artifacts. Preferred fix: update problem_statement.md (UML and textual task) to specify messageOnMilk() returns a String (and show example message like "[AnimalType] [name] is milked"), so it matches the class diagrams and the solution. Alternatively, change the solution to use boolean and update example outputs/tests accordingly — but ensure all diagrams, textual instructions, template code, and solution code use the same signature.
